I'm a patient, caring, and motivated teacher who is focused on helping you reach your goals. I'm also a very organized, punctual, and reliable person. 😀

My extensive background in theatre also adds a unique dimension to my teaching, particularly when it comes to helping students perfect their American accents. 🎭

I believe language learning is a journey. We'll do a lot of repetition and review to make sure you retain what you've learned and build a strong foundation. As a patient and caring teacher, I will take your needs into consideration when creating a lesson plan. Periodic check-ins will help you feel confident in the direction of your lessons., and I listen to your requests.
teacher_info.teaching_style:
My lessons are focused on "real-life" English, so we'll use materials such as articles, YouTube videos and podcasts. I love learning along with you, so I choose fun and informative topic to discuss. 

I believe in a balance of "correct" English, and fluency.  So, I will correct your mistakes, and encourage you to use new vocabulary and grammar. I'm a very organized person, so our lessons will be fun but structured. You'll receive detailed notes and clear homework assignments. I also believe "slow and steady wins the race." In other words, language learning is a journey, and not rushing it is important. With that in mind, we will do a lot of repetition and review. 😄

pro_course_detail.description:
Hi, my name is Hilary and I can help you prepare for TOEFL iBT Speaking. I’ve worked for TEN YEARS as a rater for TOEFL Speaking. In those ten years, I’ve heard literally thousands and thousands of test-takers answering hundreds of questions. I know this test inside and out. I know what test-takers should say and what they shouldn’t say. And unfortunately, I’ve learned that many test-takers either aren’t prepared for the test or they’ve prepared the wrong way. Either way, they end up with a lower speaking score than they should.

Many teachers and websites just GUESS what's on the test, how raters evaluate responses, and which way you should answer questions to get the best score. But guessing isn't good enough. I KNOW how you should answer these questions.

I highly recommend that you take at least five lessons with me if you really want to improve your score. I can give you a deeper understanding of the test, explain how you should answer each question, and dispel any misunderstandings you may have about TOEFL iBT Speaking. I can evaluate your current abilities accurately and pinpoint your problem areas. And I can help you to make your answers more coherent, fluent, and on-topic. 

The TOEFL really is a test of English fluency, and fluency can’t be achieved overnight, or even in a few months. My goal is to give you an honest and accurate assessment of where you’re currently at, and then give you an detailed road map to achieving your speaking fluency objectives. I’ll give you the tools you need to make sure you’re making headway and going in the right direction. 

How soon you get to your dream score depends on where you’re starting from and how hard you work to achieve your goal. If this is a journey you need to make, let’s work as partners to make it happen.

As a TOEFL iBT Speaking Rater for the past SIX years, I have learned that many of the mistakes test-takers make with speaking also crop up in the independent essay. Based on numerous discussions with a colleague who formerly rated TOEFL iBT Writing, I've developed strategies to help you get a better score in both the independent AND integrated writing tasks. 

Each of the two writing tasks requires quite different strategies and skill sets. By evaluating your essays, I can help you to figure out what issues are lowering your score and how to fix them. 

Whether you need help with the independent, integrated, or both writing tasks, I can help you organize your response more coherently, communicate your ideas more clearly, and finally achieve your dream score!

As a classroom teacher at a university Intensive English Program, I am used to guiding students of various levels in all language skills ... listening, speaking, writing, reading, grammar, and vocabulary. Classroom teachers conduct their classes with established course objectives, a structured syllabus, regular assessments, and teaching materials such as textbooks and online resources.
